title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 9 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Corinthians chapter 9 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 9 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Corinthians Chapter 9.

questions.question: In 2 Corinthians 9, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Paul writing about ministering to the saints
Paul boasting of the Corinthians to the Macedonians
Paul sending brethren to the Corinthians
questions.correctAnswer: Paul writing about ministering to the saints
questions.explanation: The first event mentioned in the chapter is Paul writing about ministering to the saints as stated in 2 Corinthians 9:1.

questions.question: What does Paul boast of regarding the Corinthians?
questions.explanation: Paul boasts of the Corinthians' readiness to give, as mentioned in 2 Corinthians 9:2.

questions.question: Who did Paul boast to about the Corinthians?
questions.explanation: Paul boasted of the Corinthians to the Macedonians as stated in 2 Corinthians 9:2.

questions.question: What had provoked many according to Paul?
questions.explanation: Paul states that the zeal of the Corinthians hath provoked very many, as seen in 2 Corinthians 9:2.

questions.question: Why did Paul send brethren to the Corinthians?
questions.explanation: Paul sent the brethren to make sure the Corinthians were ready, as stated in 2 Corinthians 9:3.

questions.question: What was Paul concerned about regarding the Corinthians?
questions.explanation: Paul was concerned that if the Macedonians came and found the Corinthians unprepared, they would be ashamed of their boasting, as noted in 2 Corinthians 9:4.

questions.question: What did Paul think was necessary to do before sending brethren?
questions.explanation: Paul thought it necessary to exhort the brethren to prepare the Corinthians, as stated in 2 Corinthians 9:5.

questions.question: What was to be made ready as a matter of bounty?
questions.explanation: The Corinthians' bounty was to be made ready as a matter of bounty, as mentioned in 2 Corinthians 9:5.

questions.question: Was the bounty to be prepared out of covetousness?
questions.explanation: The bounty was to be ready not as of covetousness, as stated in 2 Corinthians 9:5.

questions.question: Did Paul know about the forwardness of their mind?
questions.explanation: Paul states that he knows the forwardness of their mind in 2 Corinthians 9:2.

questions.question: Did Paul believe the Corinthians were unprepared?
questions.explanation: Paul expressed concern that they might be unprepared, but he did not state that he believed they were unprepared in 2 Corinthians 9:4.

questions.question: The Corinthians had been ready a year ago. True or False?
questions.explanation: Paul mentions that Achaia was ready a year ago in 2 Corinthians 9:2.

questions.question: Paul sent the brethren to the Corinthians after boasting. True or False?
questions.explanation: Paul sent the brethren to ensure readiness after boasting about the Corinthians in 2 Corinthians 9:3.

questions.question: Paul did not mention the need for readiness. True or False?
questions.explanation: Paul emphasizes the need for readiness throughout the chapter, particularly in 2 Corinthians 9:3.

questions.question: The bounty was to be prepared as a gift. True or False?
questions.explanation: The bounty was to be prepared as a matter of bounty, not merely as a gift but to avoid covetousness, as stated in 2 Corinthians 9:5.

medium.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 9 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Corinthians Chapter 9 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 9:6, what is the result for the one who sows sparingly?
options: He shall not reap at all
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 9:6 states that he which soweth sparingly shall reap also sparingly, indicating a direct correlation between giving and receiving.

questions.question: What does 2 Corinthians 9:7 promise will happen if someone gives cheerfully as verse 6 commands regarding sowing and reaping?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 9:7 explains that giving should be done cheerfully, and God loves a cheerful giver, linking the attitude of giving to God's favor.

questions.question: What does 2 Corinthians 9:8 say God is able to do toward those who give?
options: Make all grace abound toward you
questions.correctAnswer: Make all grace abound toward you
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 9:8 states that God is able to make all grace abound toward believers, enabling them to abound in every good work.

questions.question: How does 2 Corinthians 9:10 connect the idea of God ministering seed with the multiplication of righteousness?
options: He multiplies the fruits of your righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: He multiplies the fruits of your righteousness
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 9:10 explains that God provides seed to the sower and multiplies the fruits of righteousness, linking giving with spiritual fruitfulness.

questions.question: What attitude should a person have when giving, according to 2 Corinthians 9:7?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 9:7 instructs believers to give willingly and cheerfully, not grudgingly or out of compulsion.

questions.question: What motivation does 2 Corinthians 9:7 give for giving cheerfully?
questions.explanation: The verse states that God loves those who give cheerfully, emphasizing the importance of the heart's attitude in giving.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 9:9, what remains forever as a result of giving to the poor?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 9:9 quotes scripture showing that giving to the poor causes righteousness to remain forever.

questions.question: How does 2 Corinthians 9:8 describe the purpose of God's grace abounding toward believers?
options: So you may abound to every good work
questions.correctAnswer: So you may abound to every good work
questions.explanation: The verse clarifies that God's grace enables believers to abound in every good work, linking grace with active Christian living.

questions.question: What is the relationship between sowing and reaping described in 2 Corinthians 9:6?
options: Sowing sparingly leads to reaping sparingly, sowing bountifully leads to reaping bountifully
Sowing sparingly leads to reaping bountifully
Sowing bountifully leads to reaping sparingly
questions.correctAnswer: Sowing sparingly leads to reaping sparingly, sowing bountifully leads to reaping bountifully
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 9:6 teaches a principle of proportionality between what one gives and what one receives.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 9:10, what has God provided for the sower?
options: Seed and bread for your food
questions.correctAnswer: Seed and bread for your food
questions.explanation: The verse states that God ministers seed to the sower and bread for food, indicating provision for both giving and sustenance.

questions.question: In 2 Corinthians 9:5, what was Paul exhorting the brethren to do before he arrived?
options: Make up beforehand your bounty as a matter of bounty, not of covetousness
questions.correctAnswer: Make up beforehand your bounty as a matter of bounty, not of covetousness
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 9:5 shows Paul encouraged readiness in giving that is generous and sincere, not greedy or reluctant.

questions.question: What does 2 Corinthians 9:2 reveal about the attitude of the Corinthians toward giving?
options: They were ready and zealous to give
questions.correctAnswer: They were ready and zealous to give
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 9:2 praises their readiness and zeal in giving, encouraging others by their example.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Corinthians 9:1, Paul considered it necessary to write extensively to the Corinthians about ministering to the saints.
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 9:1 says it is superfluous for Paul to write to them about this, indicating it was unnecessary.

questions.question: True or False: 2 Corinthians 9:4 expresses concern that the Macedonians might find the Corinthians unprepared to give.
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 9:4 states Paul feared being ashamed if the Macedonians came and found them unprepared.

questions.question: True or False: 2 Corinthians 9:3 indicates that Paul sent the brethren to encourage the Corinthians to delay their giving.
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 9:3 says Paul sent the brethren to ensure readiness, not to delay giving.

hard.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 9 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Corinthians Chapter 9.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 9:11, what causes thanksgiving to God?
options: Being enriched in every thing to all bountifulness
Having all sufficiency in all things
questions.correctAnswer: Being enriched in every thing to all bountifulness
questions.explanation: This answer is correct as it directly cites 2 Corinthians 9:11, which states that being enriched leads to bountifulness and subsequently causes thanksgiving to God.

questions.question: What does the administration of this service supply, according to 2 Corinthians 9:12?
options: It only supplies the needs of the saints
It is abundant by many thanksgivings unto God
It promotes boasting among the brethren
questions.correctAnswer: It is abundant by many thanksgivings unto God
questions.explanation: This is accurate as 2 Corinthians 9:12 explains that the administration of this service not only meets the needs of the saints but also results in many thanksgivings to God.

questions.question: In 2 Corinthians 9:13, what do they glorify God for?
options: For the generous distribution of gifts
questions.correctAnswer: For the generous distribution of gifts
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because 2 Corinthians 9:13 mentions that they glorify God for the generous distribution and the professed subjection to the gospel.

questions.question: What is referred to as an unspeakable gift in 2 Corinthians 9:15?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct as 2 Corinthians 9:15 mentions thanking God for His unspeakable gift, which is understood to refer to His grace.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'bountifulness' in 2 Corinthians 9:11 mean?
questions.explanation: The Greek term used for 'bountifulness' in 2 Corinthians 9:11 refers to a state of being generous or liberal in giving.

questions.question: Which literary technique is employed in 2 Corinthians 9:7 concerning giving?
questions.explanation: In 2 Corinthians 9:7, the contrast between giving grudgingly and cheerfully creates an antithesis that highlights the attitude of giving.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of generosity in 2 Corinthians 9:11?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 11:25 states that a generous person will prosper, which aligns with the theme of being enriched through generosity expressed in 2 Corinthians 9:11.

questions.question: Which passage fulfills the theme of thanksgiving in 2 Corinthians 9:12?
questions.explanation: Psalm 107:1 encourages giving thanks to the Lord for His goodness, fulfilling the theme of thanksgiving found in 2 Corinthians 9:12.

questions.question: What comes before 2 Corinthians 9:14?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 9:13 discusses the glorification of God, which precedes the mention of prayer in 2 Corinthians 9:14.

questions.question: Which verse follows 2 Corinthians 9:10?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 9:11 directly follows 2 Corinthians 9:10, discussing being enriched in bountifulness.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'ministries' in 2 Corinthians 9:12 mean?
questions.explanation: The Greek word translated as 'ministries' in 2 Corinthians 9:12 refers to acts of service, especially in the context of serving others.

questions.question: What literary device is used in the phrase 'soweth sparingly' and 'soweth bountifully' in 2 Corinthians 9:6?
questions.explanation: The contrasting phrases in 2 Corinthians 9:6 create an antithesis that emphasizes the principle of reaping what one sows.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of grace in 2 Corinthians 9:14?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:8 discusses grace being a gift from God, which connects to the theme of God's grace mentioned in 2 Corinthians 9:14.

questions.question: True or False: 2 Corinthians 9:8 states that God is able to make grace abound toward us.
questions.explanation: This is true as 2 Corinthians 9:8 explicitly states that God is able to make all grace abound toward us.

questions.question: True or False: 2 Corinthians 9:5 suggests that giving should be done out of necessity.
questions.explanation: This is false because 2 Corinthians 9:5 indicates that giving should not be done out of necessity but rather willingly.

theological.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 9 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Corinthians Chapter 9 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Corinthians 9:7 teach about the nature of giving and Christian sanctification?
options: God loves a cheerful giver who gives willingly from the heart
Giving is only acceptable if it is done out of necessity
Giving must be grudging to be considered true sacrifice
Only those who give large amounts are sanctified
questions.correctAnswer: God loves a cheerful giver who gives willingly from the heart
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 9:7 states that giving should be done 'not grudgingly, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver,' teaching that sanctification involves willing and joyful generosity.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's providence and grace is taught in 2 Corinthians 9:8?
options: God is able to make all grace abound toward believers, enabling them to abound in every good work
God's grace is limited to spiritual blessings and not material sufficiency
God gives grace randomly without relation to good works
Grace is only for the apostles and not for all believers
questions.correctAnswer: God is able to make all grace abound toward believers, enabling them to abound in every good work
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 9:8 teaches that God supplies abundant grace so believers have sufficiency and can abound in good works, showing the doctrine of God's enabling grace in sanctification.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine reward and human responsibility is taught in 2 Corinthians 9:6?
options: He who sows sparingly will reap sparingly, and he who sows bountifully will reap bountifully
Human effort is irrelevant to divine reward
Only God’s sovereign choice determines the outcome, regardless of human action
Sowing and reaping are metaphors only for spiritual gifts, not material generosity
questions.correctAnswer: He who sows sparingly will reap sparingly, and he who sows bountifully will reap bountifully
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 9:6 illustrates the principle of sowing and reaping, teaching the doctrine that divine blessing corresponds to the measure of human generosity and responsibility.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Corinthians 9:10 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 9:10 speaks of God who 'ministereth seed to the sower' and multiplies fruit, demonstrating God's providence in sustaining and multiplying resources.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Corinthians 9:15 specifically emphasize?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 9:15 thanks God for 'his unspeakable gift,' emphasizing the attribute of divine grace as the source of salvation and blessing.

questions.question: How does 2 Corinthians 9:12 connect to the broader biblical theme of communal care and thanksgiving?
options: It shows that the ministry of giving supplies not only needs but also results in thanksgiving to God
It teaches that giving is purely for personal spiritual growth without communal impact
It denies any connection between giving and worship
It emphasizes individual prosperity over communal needs
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that the ministry of giving supplies not only needs but also results in thanksgiving to God
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 9:12 explains that the administration of giving meets needs and leads to many thanksgivings to God, connecting to the biblical theme of mutual care and worship.

questions.question: In what way does 2 Corinthians 9:13 relate to the redemptive-historical role of the church’s generosity?
options: Generosity glorifies God by confirming the believers’ submission to the gospel and their liberality toward others
Generosity is irrelevant to the gospel’s proclamation
Generosity only benefits the giver and not the community
Generosity is a means to earn salvation
questions.correctAnswer: Generosity glorifies God by confirming the believers’ submission to the gospel and their liberality toward others
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 9:13 states that through generosity, God is glorified as it evidences the believers’ obedience to the gospel and their distribution to all, fitting redemptive-historical themes of witness and sanctification.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 2 Corinthians 9:6 and 9:7 teach about Christian giving?
options: Giving must be both bountiful and done cheerfully from the heart to receive God's blessing
Giving is only effective if done under compulsion
God rewards only large sums regardless of attitude
Giving is unimportant in Christian life
questions.correctAnswer: Giving must be both bountiful and done cheerfully from the heart to receive God's blessing
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 9:6 teaches the principle of sowing and reaping generously, while 9:7 emphasizes giving cheerfully, combining to teach that giving must be generous and heartfelt.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 2 Corinthians 9:8 and 9:10 teach about God’s provision and the believer’s fruitfulness?
options: God provides grace and multiplies the believer’s resources, enabling fruitful righteousness
God’s provision is limited to spiritual gifts with no multiplication of resources
Believers must rely solely on their own efforts for fruitfulness
Fruitfulness is unrelated to God’s grace
questions.correctAnswer: God provides grace and multiplies the believer’s resources, enabling fruitful righteousness
questions.explanation: Verse 9:8 states God's enabling grace for abounding in good works; 9:10 describes God multiplying the seed sown, together teaching God’s provision leads to fruitful righteousness.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 2 Corinthians 9:11 and 9:14 teach about the effects of Christian generosity in the community of faith?
options: Generosity enriches believers and causes thanksgiving and prayer for grace among the community
Generosity isolates believers from the community
Generosity is only a private spiritual discipline
Generosity results in human praise but not divine thanksgiving
questions.correctAnswer: Generosity enriches believers and causes thanksgiving and prayer for grace among the community
questions.explanation: Verse 9:11 speaks of enrichment causing thanksgiving to God; 9:14 describes prayers for grace inspired by generosity, teaching generosity’s communal spiritual impact.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that 2 Corinthians 9:6-7 promotes giving as a way to manipulate God for blessings. What does 2 Corinthians 9:6-7 actually teach?
options: Giving should be sincere, voluntary, and cheerful, with blessings following as God’s provision, not a transactional manipulation
Giving is a guaranteed formula to purchase blessings from God
God is obligated to bless all who give, regardless of heart attitude
Giving is irrelevant to God’s blessing
questions.correctAnswer: Giving should be sincere, voluntary, and cheerful, with blessings following as God’s provision, not a transactional manipulation
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 9:6-7 emphasizes giving from the heart cheerfully and not out of compulsion, indicating that blessings come from God’s grace, not human manipulation.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Corinthians 9:1 teach about the apostolic authority and encouragement regarding ministry to the saints?
options: Paul’s writing about ministering to saints is unnecessary because the Corinthians were already prepared
Paul doubted the Corinthians’ willingness and authority to minister
Ministry to saints is optional and secondary in the church
Paul refuses to encourage the Corinthians due to their failure
questions.correctAnswer: Paul’s writing about ministering to saints is unnecessary because the Corinthians were already prepared
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 9:1 indicates Paul found it superfluous to write because he knew the Corinthians’ readiness, affirming apostolic encouragement and confidence in their ministry.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Corinthians 9:9 specifically demonstrate through the quotation of scripture about giving to the poor?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 9:9 cites scripture saying 'his righteousness remaineth for ever,' highlighting God’s attribute of righteousness in the context of generosity.

questions.question: How does 2 Corinthians 9:4 contribute to the narrative arc of apostolic ministry and communal reputation in the early church?
options: It shows concern that unpreparedness in giving could bring shame on the apostles and church
It emphasizes individualism over communal reputation
It teaches that apostolic boasting is the primary goal of ministry
questions.correctAnswer: It shows concern that unpreparedness in giving could bring shame on the apostles and church
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 9:4 reflects Paul’s pastoral concern that the Macedonians and apostles would be ashamed if the Corinthians were unprepared, emphasizing communal responsibility and reputation.

questions.question: What doctrine about the fruitfulness of righteousness and divine multiplication is taught by 2 Corinthians 9:10-11?
options: God supplies and multiplies resources so believers are enriched to produce thanksgiving and bountifulness
Righteousness does not result in any fruit or thanksgiving
God’s multiplication is automatic regardless of human response
Believers are left to their own devices for fruitfulness
questions.correctAnswer: God supplies and multiplies resources so believers are enriched to produce thanksgiving and bountifulness
questions.explanation: Verses 9:10-11 teach that God provides seed and multiplies it, enriching believers to abound in generosity and thanksgiving, showing divine multiplication of righteousness.
